text:
Columbus threw 73 shot attempts at Jacob Markstrom and got one past him. That was the game. The Blue Jackets had more of the even-strength chances, 38 shots on goal to Florida's 28, and by our replay of every shot they deserved to win 56% of the time. Florida won 4-1 because Markstrom saved two goals more than the shots deserved and Sam Bennett scored twice on chances that usually don't go in.

The Panthers did their damage in a two-minute burst early in the second period. Bennett opened the scoring on Florida's only power play, two minutes in, off Anton Lundell and Seth Jones. Lars Eller added a second at 4:17, set up by Carter Verhaeghe and Aaron Ekblad, and Florida's win chance went from 67% to 82%. Columbus didn't get on the board until 19 seconds were left in the period, when Ivan Provorov scored on a backhand. Provorov's return has been the Blue Jackets' good news this month, and he was their best player again.

The third was all Columbus, 1.32 expected goals (the quality of chances) to 0.39. Markstrom's biggest save came on Matthew Knies, a 22% look, and by our count he added almost half a win by himself. Then Bennett broke it open at 14:29 with a 6% wrist shot, Ekblad and Matthew Tkachuk assisting. Sam Reinhart's backhand into an empty net with 2:16 left closed it. Lundell, back after missing time, had two assists.

Cam Talbot allowed three on 27 shots, a little worse than expected, which isn't much of a complaint on a night his team couldn't finish. Columbus won 35 of 57 faceoffs and 10 takeaways to Florida's four. None of it turned into goals.

Florida has now beaten Columbus twice, by a combined 11-4, though this one was much closer than the score. The Blue Jackets' issue all season has been exactly this: decent chances, not enough of them going in. Nights like this are why.
headline: Markstrom stands in the way, Bennett does the rest
